10.text: Another result of American influence, far less pleasant, is that due to

11.text: the great destruction of animal life in the waters of Bering Sea, chiefly that

12.text: of whales, and partly also of walrus. Thus, the whalers take the whalebone,

13.text: and leave the carcass floating on the water. This wanton extermination of

14.text: the largest species of animal on earth brings with it the gradual restriction

15.text: of resources for all the natives living along the coast. The Keˊrek are starving,

16.text: because the walrus have ceased to visit the coast south of Anadyr Bay.

17.text: It is fortunate for the Maritime Chukchee and Asiatic Eskimo that the

18.text: whalers of late have ceased to hunt walrus, because it does not pay. The

19.text: walrus plays so important a part in the diet of these tribes, that without it

20.text: they might have gone the way of the Keˊrek. One of my Eskimo acquaint-

21.text: ances put it in the following simple way: “When the Americans came to us,

22.text: we had a talk with them, and we said, ‘Take the whales, but leave us the

23.text: walrus. We also want something to eat. We shall give you all the walrus-

25.text: From the native point of view, the decrease in animal life on the sea-

26.text: shore is brought about, first of all, by the infringement, on the part of the

27.text: Americans, of the well-known taboo against the burning of fuel during the

28.text: whole winter season.² For this reason the natives are generally averse to

29.text: the idea of having an American settlement in their vicinity. As another of

30.text: my Eskimo acquaintances expressed it in his broken English, “Russian king

31.text: big captain. American king big captain, not very. Speak em, sell em, twelve

32.text: miles this shore, twelve miles that shore. Twenty-four miles land down on

33.text: the beach. American man speak: ‘Give you ten thousand dollar.’ — ‘No!’ —

34.text: ‘What is the matter?’ — ‘No!’ — ‘American man plenty fire, smell im by

35.text: and by, walruses, seals, come away. Indian Point men seek em, hunt em,

36.text: no, nothing. By and by die. No! American man trade em whiskey plenty.

37.text: Indian Point men drink em, fight. No good. American man plenty s— of b—.’”
